alerts.title: ‘Nowhere is safe’: UN experts detail Ukraine war’s toll and Russia’s reach beyond its borders
alerts.summary: UN Human Rights Council-appointed experts on Monday laid out a grim picture of the human cost of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, with a spotlight on civilians facing a third wartime winter as well as the intimidation of Russians who have fled abroad.

alerts.title: ‘We are not powerless’: UN chief urges world leaders to invest in peace
alerts.summary: In a world facing rising conflicts, violence and divisions that are causing great suffering for millions of people, the UN chief on Monday called on world leaders and citizens to invest more in peace.

alerts.title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
alerts.summary: An Ebola vaccine trial is underway in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), involving frontline health workers and others involved in the response.

alerts.title: Yemen’s humanitarian crisis growing by the hour amid spike in displacement
alerts.summary: People displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen have described fleeing for their lives amid shelling and gunfire, aid agencies reported on Friday, while highlighting the dramatic increase in humanitarian needs in the country and in Djibouti, where thousands have sought shelter.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: UN peacekeeping under pressure
alerts.summary: UN peacekeepers have increasingly been sent into places where there is no peace to keep – under resourced, outgunned and exposed to violence they are not equipped to counter. The Security Council meets this afternoon in New York to confront that problem, with Secretary-General António Guterres briefing ambassadors on how to close the gap.

alerts.title: Sexual violence against civilians and POWs in Ukraine widespread and ‘abhorrent’
alerts.summary: Over 1,000 cases of sexual violence against civilians and prisoners of war (POWs) in Ukraine have been documented from the start of Russia’s invasion to the end of July this year.

alerts.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
alerts.summary: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s transition in the spotlight
alerts.summary: While Syria is making progress in its political transition, the Security Council is meeting to hear briefings and discuss the situation on the ground, including recent reports of deadly armed clashes with an ISIS-affiliate terrorist group in the south and protests over rising fuel prices.&nbsp;

alerts.title: Yemen escalation displaces more than 57,000 children: UNICEF
alerts.summary: Renewed fighting in Yemen is deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis in a country where more than 12 million children depend on aid, after more than a decade of conflict.

alerts.title: UN fact-finding mission on Iran focuses on plight of civilians
alerts.summary: The Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran confirmed that civilians in the country suffered serious human rights violations and “crimes against humanity committed by their government,” while finding "reasonable grounds" to believe that the United States committed “war crimes” in the context of its ongoing conflict with the Islamic Republic.

alerts.title: Gaza: At least 20 killed in deadly building collapse, search for survivors continues
alerts.summary: Search and rescue operations continued in Gaza City on Wednesday following the collapse of a bombed-out building that killed at least 20 people, according to reports.

alerts.title: Who should set the rules for AI? The UN is pushing for a safer digital future
alerts.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly, raising questions about how societies and governments can capture its benefits while managing risks that often extend beyond national borders.

alerts.title: World News in Brief: Shipping alert from IMO, democracy vanishing in Nicaragua, alert over political ‘denialism’
alerts.summary: Amid a rising number of attacks on shipping in key waterways in the Middle East linked to the US-Iran war, the head of UN maritime agency, Mr. Arsenio Dominguez, has insisted that the conflict is not a “pretext” to target “innocent seafarers”.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: ‘Being a woman is a crime in Afghanistan,’ civil society briefer declares
alerts.summary: Since the Taliban returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021, the continuing presence of terrorist groups as well as rights violations against women and girls are a growing concern as the Security Council met Wednesday to hear latest developments, including from a civil society representative who said being born as a woman in the country “is a crime”. Follow full coverage here.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Rising violence triggers emergency meeting on Yemen
alerts.summary: Amid rising violence in Yemen, the Security Council met in emergency session on Tuesday to discuss the situation surrounding the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait shipping route as UN agencies warn of rising displacement, including thousands of Yemenis fleeing to Djibouti. UN News app users can follow here.

alerts.title: Escalating conflict drives new displacement in Yemen
alerts.summary: The escalating conflict in Yemen is choking off aid shipments and driving fresh displacement, including to nearby Djibouti, with UN agencies reporting on Tuesday that nearly 100,000 people have been displaced since fighting intensified earlier this month.

alerts.title: Gaza remains recovery points to possible war crimes, says UN rights chief
alerts.summary: Bodies are still being pulled from the rubble of Gaza, three years after Israeli bombardment flattened entire neighbourhoods – most of them women and children.&nbsp;&nbsp;

alerts.title: Back to school in Haiti: ‘Madame, can you stop what the gangs are doing to us?’
alerts.summary: When UNICEF’s Representative in Haiti Geetanjali Narayan stepped into a classroom in Port-au-Prince at the start of the new school year, she asked the children a simple question: What did they most need from the UN children’s agency?

alerts.title: World fears major war more than any other global risk, UN survey finds
alerts.summary: Two years ago, the idea of a large-scale war breaking out felt like a distant hypothetical to the experts who help chart the world’s dangers. Today it tops their list of fears, according to a new UN Global Risk Report.

alerts.title: ‘Super El Niño’ deepens hunger crisis in South Sudan – WFP
alerts.summary: The already dire hunger crisis in South Sudan is becoming increasingly critical as violence, extreme weather and dwindling aid leave millions without enough food, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Tuesday.

alerts.title: Six UN staff killed in Gaza school strike; Lebanon violations mount
alerts.summary: Israeli strikes killed six UN workers and civilians at a school sheltering displaced families in Gaza as needs grow, according to the UN agency for Palestine refugees, UNRWA.

alerts.title: Civilians bear the brunt, with deadly US strikes in Iran and thousands displaced in Yemen
alerts.summary: Independent UN human rights investigators called for an immediate cessation of hostilities on Monday following a series of United States airstrikes on Iran in recent weeks that have killed civilians as tensions ripple through the region.

alerts.title: UN agencies warn humanitarian system in Sudan ‘could collapse’
alerts.summary: UN aid agencies on Monday said they may be forced to scale back humanitarian aid in Sudan – home of the world’s worst hunger and displacement crisis – due to funding shortfalls.

alerts.title: IAEA chief underscores commitment to nuclear safety and verification
alerts.summary: The Director General of the UN nuclear watchdog, IAEA, opened its 70th General Conference on Monday in Vienna with a message full of optimism, stressing that despite the many difficulties and tensions the world is witnessing a “common spirit of dedication” which still guides their work.

alerts.title: Married at 13, pregnant and starving: Child brides of Yemen
alerts.summary: Fatimah* was 13 when she was married off to an older man. Two years later, she gave birth to twin daughters.

alerts.title: ‘Where do we go?’: How Israel’s ‘yellow line’ is closing in on Palestinians
alerts.summary: Ola&nbsp;Ishtiwi&nbsp;sits with her children in front of&nbsp;the&nbsp;remains of her home in the Al-Tuffah neighbourhood in eastern Gaza City, a few metres away from&nbsp;a series of&nbsp;painted cement blocks&nbsp;Israel has&nbsp;placed to mark what has become known as the&nbsp;“yellow line”.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Ambassadors mark 9/11 with counter-terrorism push on AI and drones
alerts.summary: The Security Council met to mark 25 years since the 9/11 attacks with a briefing on counter-terrorism as ambassadors take stock of a threat that has morphed dramatically since resolution 1373 built the council's counter-terrorism machinery in 2001. Briefers highlighted militants' growing use of artificial intelligence, drones and encrypted platforms for recruitment and attack planning.

alerts.title: Terrorist propaganda is outpacing global efforts to stop it, UN report finds
alerts.summary: Terrorist groups are recruiting, raising money and even planning operations through propaganda that is now “embedded” in every stage of their work, a new UN report warns – and governments are struggling to keep pace.&nbsp;

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Fresh attacks prompt emergency meeting on Yemen
alerts.summary: On the heels of reported Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on Tuesday and the capture of another key port by the militants on Yemen’s Red Sea coast – including the seizure of eight UN vehicles from a key aid hub there – the Security Council is meeting on Thursday at 3pm in New York to discuss the latest developments.

alerts.title: Ukraine: Drone attacks on Chornobyl are ‘gambling with the safety of millions of people’
alerts.summary: A drone strike on the protective structure at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant could have endangered the safety of millions of people, UN Development Programme (UNDP) Administrator Alexander De Croo told reporters via video link from Kyiv on Thursday.

alerts.title: ‘An assault on humanity itself’: Guterres pays tribute to 9/11 victims, survivors and first responders
alerts.summary: Twenty-five years ago, the heinous terrorist attacks of 11 September 2001 against the United States claimed thousands of lives and represented “an assault on humanity itself”, the UN chief said on Thursday.

alerts.title: Human cost of violence in South Sudan ‘continues to grow’
alerts.summary: Independent human rights investigators voiced deep concern over growing risks to both civilians and South Sudan’s political transition following their latest fact-finding mission to the world’s youngest nation – their 14th in a decade.&nbsp;

alerts.title: UN hails Libya election deal as Security Council urges Libyans to seize the moment
alerts.summary: The UN Security Council has welcomed a breakthrough agreement between Libya's rival political blocs, calling it "an important step" towards the country's first national elections in over a decade – while pressing all sides to move quickly from paper to practice.

alerts.title: Guterres urges leaders to invest in peace as conflicts deepen
alerts.summary: The UN Secretary-General appealed on Wednesday for world leaders to invest in peace as violence, division and conflict exacerbate suffering worldwide.&nbsp;

alerts.title: Record number of attacks on education, global fund warns
alerts.summary: While September traditionally marks the start of the school year across the northern hemisphere, a staggering 93 million children are not in class at all amid an unprecedented number of attacks on learning, education experts warned on Wednesday.

alerts.title: UN chief demands Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon amid Nabatieh escalation
alerts.summary: The Secretary-General has condemned mounting civilian casualties in southern Lebanon and called on Israel to withdraw its forces from Lebanese territory, as fighting intensifies in and around Nabatieh.

alerts.title: Syria’s transition hinges on justice for all, UN Human Rights Council hears
alerts.summary: A successful and lasting transition in Syria requires comprehensive accountability, inclusion and guarantees that violations will not be repeated, UN independent investigators told the Human Rights Council in Geneva on Tuesday.

alerts.title: In Gaza, women-headed households face ‘impossible choices’ to survive
alerts.summary: In war-torn Gaza, a growing number of women-headed households face “impossible decisions” every day, amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and still-scarce resources, UN humanitarians said on Tuesday.&nbsp;

alerts.title: Ships and seafarers increasingly caught in the crossfire of unrelated wars
alerts.summary: The global shipping industry is facing a "genuinely unprecedented" convergence of maritime crises, with vessels and seafarers increasingly used as “leverage” in conflicts that have nothing to do with them.

alerts.title: AI: Türk urges action before it becomes an ‘existential risk to humanity’
alerts.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk added his voice on Monday to growing calls for greater AI controls, warning that the revolutionary technology could become an “existential risk to humanity” if left unchecked.

alerts.title: West Bank: UN rights report warns of forcible displacement from three refugee camps
alerts.summary: Israeli security forces forcibly displaced the entire population of three Palestine refugee camps in the occupied West Bank in January and February last year – and continue to prevent their return, in violation of international law, according to a new report&nbsp;by the UN human rights office, OHCHR.

alerts.title: Lebanon–Israel tensions escalate as Gaza sees major aid delivery
alerts.summary: Peacekeepers in Lebanon have reported a marked deterioration in the security situation along the Blue Line of separation, with Israeli forces intensifying their military footprint in violation of a landmark Security Council resolution, UN Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Thursday.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Addressing the legacy of Syria’s chemical weapons
alerts.summary: Following revelations from the UN nuclear watchdog that the former Syrian regime failed to report holding nuclear material and the discovery in May of an undeclared chemical weapons cache, the Security Council met Thursday to be briefed on the latest developments and discuss the way ahead.

alerts.title: ‘Don’t give up’: Syrian women’s ongoing search for the missing
alerts.summary: Yasmin Al-Mashaan lost five brothers during more than a decade of conflict in Syria. Two were forcibly disappeared. Three were killed during peaceful demonstrations or by snipers loyal to the Bashar Al-Assad regime.

alerts.title: Decades of war have left ‘depth and breadth’ of trauma across Afghanistan, UN finds
alerts.summary: Victims of Afghanistan’s decades-long armed conflict continue to suffer profound physical, psychological, social and economic consequences, often without access to justice, reparation or formal acknowledgement of the harm done to them, according to a&nbsp;new UN report.

alerts.title: Food aid cutback in the occupied West Bank as health fears grow in Gaza
alerts.summary: Lack of funding has forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash aid to families in the West Bank by half even though needs have more than doubled over the past two years.

alerts.title: Four children killed as separate attacks in Gaza destroy aid supplies
alerts.summary: Israeli attacks killed four children and destroyed humanitarian aid supplies in what turned out to be a deadly week in war-ravaged Gaza, the UN emergency relief agency, OCHA, said on Friday.

alerts.title: Aid reaches hundreds of thousands in Gaza amid severe food insecurity
alerts.summary: As hunger deepens across Gaza, humanitarian agencies continue to deliver food and other essential supplies to families in need.

alerts.title: After Israeli seizure of Kalandia training centre, UNRWA warns of impact on youth
alerts.summary: The seizure of a vocational training centre in occupied East Jerusalem has left hundreds of Palestinian young people without access to skills and training that could help shape their futures.&nbsp;

alerts.title: Lebanon: Civilian risks grow as military activity continues, UN says
alerts.summary: Damaged roads, disrupted services and ongoing military activity continue to put civilians at risk in south Lebanon as strikes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah continue, according to the UN’s peacekeeping mission in the country (UNIFIL).

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Tracking Syria’s transition
alerts.summary: As Damascus continues to rebuild after more than a decade of war – from the recent dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces to the United States’ removal of Syria from its sponsors of terrorism list – a top UN official warned the Security Council on Thursday that international support can help tackle outstanding challenges. UN News app users can follow here.

alerts.title: Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster
alerts.summary: Amid reports that hundreds of people are still missing in Nepal and China after a floodwater surge slammed into towns and villages on Wednesday, aid teams have been working to reach communities cut off by the disaster.

alerts.title: Security Council LIVE: Rising tensions in Gaza, West Bank
alerts.summary: Amid illegal Israeli settlement surges, continued attacks in Gaza and the West Bank alongside tensions throughout Occupied Palestinian Territory, the Security Council discussed the latest developments on Wednesday, with the UN Special Envoy stressing that “human dignity must be at the centre of all efforts” to overcome the current fragile ceasefire and continued suffering. UN News app users can follow here.

alerts.title: Gaza: Children still at risk despite drop in acute hunger
alerts.summary: Among tent cities pitched on the rubble of destroyed homes in Gaza, children are, by one measure, finally getting enough to eat. By another, however, many of them may never fully recover, according to a new study by the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) released on Monday.
